businessId.meta.title: What is a Business ID?
businessId.meta.description: A Business ID is the verified profile behind a Startup Value Index score: identity, evidence and capabilities in one record. Five levels, consent-based sharing.
businessId.eyebrow: The verified profile behind your score
businessId.headline: One Business. One Trusted Identity.
businessId.subhead: A Business ID is the verified profile behind your Startup Value Index score — your evidence, verification level and capabilities in one record — so investors, accelerators and grant panels can trust what you claim, without re-verifying it every time.
businessId.what.title: What a Business ID is
businessId.what.intro: Four ingredients bundled into one reusable record — verified once, presented on your terms, revocable at any time.
businessId.what.identity.title: Verified identity
businessId.what.identity.body: ASIC/ABR/ABN checked, directors matched, domain and email owner confirmed. The identity anchor for everything else on your profile.
businessId.what.evidence.title: Evidence
businessId.what.evidence.body: Traction, financials, contracts, IP — stored encrypted, hash-anchored in an audit log, cited inline in your Trust Report.
businessId.what.capabilities.title: Capabilities
businessId.what.capabilities.body: What your business can actually do — sector, offering, team skills, tooling — scored on the 13-area rubric.
businessId.what.reusable.title: Reusable
businessId.what.reusable.body: One record, many share packages. Send a signed link to an investor today, a buyer tomorrow, a grant panel next week — always current, never re-typed.
businessId.levels.title: Five verification levels
businessId.levels.intro: Each level adds a checkable claim on top of the previous one. Public /id/{slug} profiles surface the badge for the level you have reached.
businessId.level1.title: L1 — Self-declared
businessId.level1.body: You have created a Business ID with a name, jurisdiction hint and email. Not sufficient for a public profile.
businessId.level2.title: L2 — Identity verified
businessId.level2.body: ASIC/ABR/ABN record matched, domain ownership confirmed, email owner verified. Minimum bar for a public /id/{slug} profile.
businessId.level3.title: L3 — Financials attested
businessId.level3.body: Financial statements attested by a qualified accountant (CA/CPA/IPA in AU, equivalent overseas). Practical bar for investor and procurement diligence.
businessId.level4.title: L4 — Independently audited
businessId.level4.body: Financial statements audited by an independent registered auditor. Required for Series A+ diligence and material procurement contracts.
businessId.level5.title: L5 — Cross-jurisdictional
businessId.level5.body: Evidence and verification present in a second jurisdiction (used by the AU-VN corridor cohort). Includes DKKD/MST alongside ASIC/ABR.
businessId.pillars.title: 13-area analysis — 4 pillars
businessId.pillars.intro: The same 13-area rubric applies to every Business ID. Investors compare apples with apples; founders know exactly which areas need evidence.
businessId.pillar1.title: Leadership & People
businessId.pillar1.a2: Culture, org design and hiring pipeline
businessId.pillar2.title: Strategy & Commercial
businessId.pillar3.title: Ops & Performance
businessId.pillar4.title: Tech & Digital
businessId.sharing.title: How sharing works
businessId.sharing.consent.title: Consent-based
businessId.sharing.consent.body: Nothing on your Business ID leaves your control unless you create a share package. Each package selects specific evidence and audiences.
businessId.sharing.expiry.title: Time-limited
businessId.sharing.expiry.body: Every share link carries an expiry (default 30 days). Recipients see a countdown. After expiry, the link 404s — no accidental long tails.
businessId.sharing.revocation.title: Revocable, audited
businessId.sharing.revocation.body: Revoke instantly at any time. Every view is logged with timestamp, IP, and (if the viewer is signed in) their Business ID — hash-chained for tamper evidence.
businessId.badge.title: Badge widget
businessId.badge.intro: Embed your verified badge on your website, LinkedIn or email signature. Renders your current verification level, last update date, and a link to your public /id/{slug} profile — updates in real time when your level changes.
businessId.badge.caption: Sample badge: Verified Business ID · Level 3 · updated Jul 2026. Copy the embed snippet from your dashboard.
businessId.cta.title: Create Your Business ID
businessId.disclaimer: Nothing on this page is financial or legal advice. Verification confirms what the record says, not the underlying business decision. {entityStatutoryLine}.

solutions.accelerator.eyebrow: BlockID Cohort — for accelerators, incubators and innovation programs
solutions.accelerator.headline: Turn your next startup intake into a comparable, evidence-backed cohort.
solutions.accelerator.persona: Score applicants consistently, identify the companies that need deeper review, target mentor support and show sponsors measurable progress from intake to demo day.
solutions.accelerator.lede: Your committee decides. BlockID makes the first pass consistent.
solutions.accelerator.support: One rubric, an evidence confidence level per startup and a cohort table your reviewers can sort.
solutions.accelerator.problem.line1: Your applicants arrive in different formats.
solutions.accelerator.problem.resolution: BlockID creates one consistent assessment layer.
solutions.accelerator.benefits.title: What a program gets
solutions.accelerator.benefit1.title: One consistent assessment layer
solutions.accelerator.benefit1.body: Every applicant is assessed on the same 8 SVI dimensions across 12 growth phases, with an evidence ladder and a confidence level, so two startups side by side is a real comparison. Batch scoring queues a whole application round on one rubric — rubric weights re-rank the display — and lands in a cohort table you can sort and download as CSV.
solutions.accelerator.benefit2.title: Evidence, not pitch polish
solutions.accelerator.benefit2.body: Claims are checked against the startup's own evidence and unsupported claims are flagged, so reviewers know where to look before the interview and every founder receives the same kind of feedback.
solutions.accelerator.benefit3.title: Progress you can show
solutions.accelerator.benefit3.body: Evidence completion and re-scoring make movement between sessions visible; the Cohort Report and the CSV export are assembled from the record, not from memory. {principle}
solutions.accelerator.journey.title: Six stages, one assessment layer
solutions.accelerator.journey.lede: Every bullet below ships today. Nothing here is a roadmap.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.head: Intake
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.b1: Your own intake link at /apply/<slug>, with deck upload and the startup URL on the form.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.b2: Import an existing cohort as CSV — company, URL, contact e-mail, stage, sector, deck link — with a validation report and dedupe by ABN or domain.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.b3: Founder consent captured on submission — each founder can claim their own score.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.head: Assessment
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.b1: Every applicant assessed on the common rubric with the evidence ladder and a confidence level.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.b2: One Startup Value Index per startup, with evidence confidence, verification level and the change since the last snapshot beside it.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.b3: Cohort snapshots on completion and on demand, so movement between sessions is a number, not a memory.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.head: Selection
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.b1: A cohort table with SVI, confidence, verification, change, strongest and weakest dimension, evidence gaps and review status — filter by stage, sector, score range or verification.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.b2: Shortlist, decision and conviction per startup; a reviewer may override a dimension score with a reason code, shown beside the model score and never replacing it.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.b3: Feedback letters to non-selected applicants — previewed first, sent only on confirm, and only once at least three submitted assessments from two or more organisations exist for the startup, so no reviewer is identifiable.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step4.head: Program
solutions.accelerator.journey.step4.b1: Progress radar and evidence completion per startup show mentors where to spend the hour.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step4.b2: A mentor-gap list per startup: the weakest dimension and the evidence that would lift it.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step4.b3: Re-scoring as evidence lands, so movement between sessions is visible.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step5.head: Demo day
solutions.accelerator.journey.step5.b1: A BlockID Dossier / IC memo per startup, built from the evidence.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step5.b2: Founders share a live profile instead of a PDF.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step5.b3: A demo-day pack — one page per selected startup with its Assessment Card, top strengths and top gaps.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step6.head: Sponsor reporting
solutions.accelerator.journey.step6.b1: The Cohort Report assembled from the cohort record: movement, improvement per dimension, benchmark with n, evidence completion, outputs, reviewer signature.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step6.b2: PDF and CSV export of the Cohort Report, plus the CSV export of the cohort table.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step6.b3: Pilot success metrics captured in the workspace — review time, evaluator consistency, satisfaction, renewal intent.
solutions.accelerator.statement.title: Humans make the decision
solutions.accelerator.statement.body: BlockID structures the evidence and standardises the first-pass analysis. Humans make the decision.

solutions.accelerator.faq.title: Frequently asked
solutions.accelerator.faq.q1: Can we score a whole application round in one run?
solutions.accelerator.faq.a1: Yes. Applicants arrive through your intake link, or you tick the startups in your evaluations workspace and choose Batch score. Every company gets a full Trusted Business Report on the same rubric and you get a sortable cohort table — SVI, weighted score, stage, movement since the last score, top strength and top gap per startup — plus a CSV export.
solutions.accelerator.faq.q2: Can our sponsors see the underlying startups?
solutions.accelerator.faq.a2: Only what you or the founder chooses to share — founder-consented access tiers control who sees what. Every Programs plan includes the Cohort Report per cohort: cohort movement, improvement per dimension, benchmark with n, evidence completion, outputs, a one-line read on each startup and a reviewer signature, exported as HTML, PDF or CSV.
solutions.accelerator.faq.q3: What does the pilot cost, and what comes after it?
solutions.accelerator.faq.a3: The Cohort Validation Pilot is a one-off, priced above and shown again before you pay, GST-inclusive with an ATO tax invoice. Programs that continue move to Cohort 25 at {cohortAnnualPrice} a year or Cohort 100 at {cohort100AnnualPrice} a year, both with a 14-day free trial, card required. Programs that need SSO, unlimited seats or white-label reports talk to us through Contact Sales.

compare.h1: BlockID vs ChatGPT vs a valuer — how to evaluate an Australian startup
compare.lede.all: Three ways to form a view on a startup before you back it, admit it to a cohort or advise it: paste the deck into a chatbot, commission an independent valuation, or run it through BlockID. Each is right for something. This page says what.
compare.lede.chatgpt: If you already screen deals with ChatGPT, this is the honest comparison: where a general chatbot is genuinely useful, and where a fixed rubric, the startup's own evidence and an audit trail change the answer.
compare.lede.valuers: An independent valuation is the right instrument for a transaction, a dispute or a tax event. For screening, tracking and advising, most evaluators need something faster, cheaper and repeatable. Here is how the two differ, and when you still need the valuer.
compare.cta.note: The trial is 7 days, card required, cancel anytime. Nothing is billed if you cancel before day 7. Scout {scoutPrice}, Firm {firmPrice}, Program {programPrice} a month, all inc. GST.

compare.fair.title: What ChatGPT is great for
compare.fair.intro: We use general models too, and this page would be dishonest without saying where they win.
compare.fair.1.title: Building the product
compare.fair.1.body: Code, architecture, debugging, documentation. A general model is a very good engineer at your elbow.
compare.fair.2.title: Drafting
compare.fair.2.body: Investor updates, memos, policies, cold emails. Give it your facts and it writes the first version faster than anyone.
compare.fair.3.title: Brainstorming
compare.fair.3.body: Objections to a thesis, questions for a founder call, adjacent markets, names. Breadth on demand.
compare.fair.outro: What it cannot do is hold one rubric across a pipeline, remember a startup's evidence next week, or show you which claim was supported. That is the job BlockID is built for, and the two work well together.

compare.faq.title: Frequently asked
compare.faq.q2: When do I still need an independent valuer?
compare.faq.a2: For anything that has to stand on its own in a transaction, a dispute, a tax matter or a court: a share buy-back, a family-law settlement, an employee share scheme valuation for the ATO, an expert report. A Trusted Business Report is a screening and tracking instrument, not a formal valuation, and it says so on every page.
compare.faq.q3: Is a Trusted Business Report a substitute for due diligence?
compare.faq.a3: No. It is a triage layer built from what the founder supplied and what is publicly available, audited for unsupported claims. It tells you where to look; it does not replace the looking. Nothing on the platform is financial, investment or legal advice.

compare.sources.title: Sources
compare.sources.intro: Cited by name, not linked. Prices are published list prices as of September 2026.
compare.sources.1: developmentcorporate.com (2026) — general models give systematically different verdicts on identical decks (GPT-4o vs Claude) and hallucinate founder histories, competitors and market figures; 85% of VCs use AI daily, 12% with a governed workflow.
compare.sources.2: MicroVentures — AI can hallucinate or invent facts, carries confirmation bias, and gives limited information on how it reached a conclusion; use it only with human intervention.
compare.sources.3: VC Lab (July 2026) — general models can confidently produce wrong information; do not upload confidential documents without checking the data policy.
compare.sources.4: VCBench, arXiv 2509.14448 — language models beat human precision only when given a consistent, anonymised rubric.
compare.sources.5: Multi-agent VC due-diligence framework, arXiv 2605.13110 — single-prompt language models lack role separation and evidence tracing.
compare.sources.prices: Price anchors — professionalbusinessvaluers.com.au (startup valuation from A$2,985 inc. GST); abva.com.au (A$3,990 + GST); equidam.com (Advanced US$412, Expert US$1,063); valutico.com (about US$7,000 a year); kruncher.com (US$499 a month, about US$5 an analysis); pitchbook.com (about US$15–20k a seat a year); affinity.co (US$2,000–2,700 a seat a year); crunchbase.com (Pro US$49 a month); openai.com (ChatGPT Plus US$20 a month; Enterprise about US$45–75 a seat with a roughly 150-seat minimum); perplexity.ai (Enterprise US$40 a seat).

calibration.rho.intro: ρ = 1 would mean the SVI order exactly matches the round-size order; 0 means no relationship. Intervals are percentile bootstraps of {resamples} seeded resamples. A stage needs at least {minN} rows to get its own ρ.

calibration.outcomes.title: Score → outcome calibration
calibration.outcomes.intro: For every company on the BlockID record: the band it was in at its first snapshot of a quarter, and whether a confirmed outcome — a round, a grant, a program selection, revenue growth, a release, a stage change — followed at least {horizon} days later. Published per cohort (stage × quarter) under the same n-rules as every benchmark: nothing under 10 companies, indicative from 10, a 95 % interval from 30. An association across companies, never a forecast for one.
calibration.outcomes.empty.title: Fewer than 10 companies with a confirmed outcome — nothing published yet
calibration.outcomes.empty.body: Outcomes are recorded by founders on their own record and by evaluators on the dossier, or proposed from public registers, connected revenue and cohort decisions — and confirmed by a person, never automatically. The first cohort is published by the weekly run as soon as ten companies in one stage and one quarter have had {horizon} days of follow-up. Until then there is nothing to show: no number is better than a made-up one.

meta.methodology.title: Methodology — how the Startup Value Index is scored
meta.methodology.description: The 8 SVI dimensions and their owner agents, the evidence ladder, ABN verification levels, the hash-chained audit log and how every score is versioned.
methodology.title: How the Startup Value Index is scored — and what stops it being gamed
methodology.subtitle: Eight dimensions, one evidence ladder, a verification level per business and an audit trail nobody can quietly edit. This page states the rules the engine actually runs; the calibration page shows how well they hold up.
methodology.dims.title: What the index measures
methodology.dims.intro: Every SVI score is a composite of these eight dimensions. Each has one accountable C-level agent and a fixed set of evaluation criteria. The names here are read from the same table the engine, the report chapters and the evaluator dossier use — they cannot drift apart.
methodology.dims.weightsNote: Dimension weights are shown to authenticated evaluators inside a report, not published here — a public weight table is a recipe for writing to the rubric rather than building the company.
methodology.ladder.title: How much a claim is worth depends on who can check it
methodology.ladder.intro: Every signal the engine reads carries a confidence level. The level scales how far the dimension score moves the index: a self-declared claim moves it a fifth as far as a third-party-verified one.
methodology.ladder.level.self_declared: The founder said so — text in a description, a form or a deck.
methodology.ladder.level.public_url: A public page we can open backs the claim (website, LinkedIn, app-store listing).
methodology.ladder.level.document_upload: A document is on file — deck, contract, cap table, bank statement — but nobody outside the company has checked it.
methodology.ladder.level.connected_sourc: Read by machine from the source of record over OAuth: GitHub, Google Analytics, Xero, Stripe customers.
methodology.ladder.level.transaction_dat: Money that moved — Stripe or Xero revenue and payouts, pulled from the ledger, not typed in.
methodology.ladder.level.third_party_ver: A named BlockID reviewer checked the evidence against an external record (ABR, ASIC, a signed contract) and signed the row.
methodology.caps.title: Who may set which level
methodology.caps.intro: The level is capped by the origin of the evidence, never by what the evidence says. Writing "audited" or "ASIC-registered" in a description does not raise anything.
methodology.caps.founder_text.rule: Prose never grades itself: a description is self-declared, or public-URL when it links to a page we can open. Writing "ASIC audit" changes nothing.
methodology.caps.founder_upload.rule: An upload counts as a document. It cannot post itself as connected, transactional or third-party verified.
methodology.caps.connector.rule: Machine-read from the source of record via OAuth; revenue and payouts are transaction data, everything else is a connected source.
methodology.caps.reviewer.rule: Only a named human reviewer can mark a row third-party verified, after the founder requests review. The approval is audit-logged.
methodology.verification.title: Six rungs from "no ABN" to continuous monitoring
methodology.verification.intro: Separately from the evidence on each claim, the business itself sits on a verification ladder. The rung is recomputed from the inputs every time — an ABN that goes Cancelled or an attestation that lapses drops the level, it is never grandfathered.
methodology.verification.col.label: Name
methodology.verification.multiplierNote: The multiplier scales the evidence confidence between {min} and {max}. It is bounded: a business at L5 whose evidence is all self-declared is still scored as self-declared — verification says the company is real, not that its claims are proven.
methodology.audit.title: Every change is hash-chained
methodology.audit.p1: Every mutating API call — an upload, a score, a reviewer decision, a share — writes one row to an append-only audit log. Postgres computes each row's hash from its content and the previous row's hash, so editing or deleting a row breaks every hash after it.
methodology.audit.p2: A nightly job re-computes the whole chain and cross-checks the last verified checkpoint. The result is published on the public status page as audit_chain: ok, broken or unknown.
methodology.audit.p3: Reviewer approvals, connector syncs and rescoring all live in this log, which is what lets a report state who verified what and when.
methodology.provenance.title: Which model wrote which chapter is on the record
methodology.provenance.p1: The deterministic score never touches a language model. Narrative chapters do, and every run records the model that produced each chapter and an auditor stamp: whether the text is grounded in the evidence rows, how many statements went uncited, and whether the auditor revised it.
methodology.provenance.p2: We do not make claims about any vendor's model being better than another's. Models are routed by availability and cost and can change between runs; the record of which one ran does not.
methodology.versioning.title: Three version numbers travel with every report
methodology.versioning.note: A stored report keeps the versions it was produced with, so an old report is never silently re-scored by a newer rule set.
methodology.data.title: Data ownership
methodology.sources.title: Open Australian data behind the score
methodology.sources.intro: Three open Commonwealth registers are bulk-ingested under their published licences and matched to a startup only by its verified ABN: the Australian Business Register (entity status, age, GST), GrantConnect grant awards and the ATO R&D Tax Incentive transparency report. Rows from these registers land at the connected_source rung of the evidence ladder, never higher. Commercial reports are cited with a link only, never copied.
methodology.sources.attributionNote: Attribution statements are printed exactly as each licence requires. Register data describes the legal entity, not the founder; the R&D register figure is shown as a band with the register’s own value, never re-estimated.
methodology.sources.cohortNote: Cohort percentiles use at least 20 peers. When fewer than 20 scored startups exist at a stage, the register cohort (ABR entity age, GST, grants, R&D registration) is used and labelled as such; below 20 there too, a static benchmark is shown and labelled an estimate.
methodology.calibration.title: How well the score tracks outcomes
methodology.calibration.body: The score is only worth publishing if it is checked against what actually happened. The calibration page reports the backtest: index at first score versus raise, revenue and survival outcomes on the AU cohort.
methodology.governance.title: How the score is governed
methodology.governance.body: Dimension definitions, the weight policy, the version history and change policy, benchmark publication rules (no percentile below n = 10, always with n), how conflicting claims are handled, how human review and overrides are logged, and how corrections, appeals and re-scores work — written for program managers, investment committees and their auditors.
methodology.governance.versionsLink: Version history — what changed in each version and its effect on comparability →
methodology.hitl.title: Who decides
methodology.hitl.body: BlockID structures the evidence and standardises the first-pass analysis. Humans make the decision.
methodology.hitl.detail: The engine produces the assessment — the score, its ledger, the evidence behind each dimension and the gaps. The program's committee, the investor or the founder records the decision. Reviewer approvals and any override are written to the audit log; automation never decides.
